findings.doc_quote: triggered by hassette reload , or by config changes when automatic reloads are on
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/cli/__init__.py:74-75,114 — apps_app = App(name="app", ...); app.command(apps_app); apps_app.command(cmd_app_reload, name="reload"). `uv run hassette --help` lists no top-level `reload` command. `uv run hassette app reload --help` prints `Usage: hassette app reload [OPTIONS] KEY [ARGS]`, with KEY required.
findings.explanation: There is no `hassette reload` command. Reload is a subcommand of `app` and takes a required app key.
findings.suggested_fix: triggered by `hassette app reload <key>`, or by config changes when automatic reloads are on

findings.doc_quote: if_exists matters most in on_initialize , which re-runs on app reload
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/core/app_lifecycle_start_stop.py:355,359 — reload_app runs `_stop_app_unlocked` then `_start_app_unlocked`. src/hassette/core/app_factory.py:191 — `app_instance = app_class(` builds a new instance. src/hassette/app/app.py:158 — `self.scheduler = self.add_child(Scheduler)`. src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:147 — `self._jobs_by_name = {}`. src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:185-188 — Scheduler.on_shutdown calls `await self.remove_all_jobs()`, and remove_all_jobs clears `_jobs_by_name` (scheduler.py:386).
findings.explanation: Reload stops the app, which removes all its jobs, then creates a new App with a new Scheduler and an empty name registry. `on_initialize` therefore runs against no existing jobs, and the duplicate check in `_add_job` (scheduler.py:287) finds nothing. Plain registration with the default `if_exists="error"` does not raise on reload. The same premise appears in the line 158 snippet comment ('Safe to call on every reload — won't create duplicates') and in line 160's skip/replace guidance. Severity is low because adding `if_exists` is harmless, but the page teaches a wrong mental model. This comes from reading the code path; I did not run a live reload.
findings.suggested_fix: A reload stops the app and removes its jobs, then runs on_initialize on a new instance, so reloads don't collide and no if_exists is needed for them. if_exists matters when the same name is registered twice during one instance's lifetime, for example from a handler that re-registers a job or a one-shot job re-arming itself.

findings.doc_quote: The monitoring UI shows this record alongside predicate_description and human_description on the job.
findings.code_evidence: frontend/src/components/app-detail/job-detail.tsx:210 — `const predicateDescription = job.human_description || job.predicate_description || null;`. src/hassette/core/scheduler_service.py:231-236 — when a predicate exists, human_description is set from `summarize()` or `callable_stable_name(job.predicate)`.
findings.explanation: The job detail view renders one description, not both. It uses human_description and falls back to predicate_description only if human_description is empty. The registration code populates human_description for any job with a predicate. Both fields do exist on the job payload (wire/src/hassette_wire/telemetry.py:146,149).
findings.suggested_fix: The monitoring UI shows this record, and the job detail view shows the predicate's description (human_description, falling back to predicate_description).

summary: The page is highly accurate on signatures, defaults, exceptions, trigger behaviour, where= semantics, and the if_exists match list; all of these were checked against the code, and croniter's 6-field order and the predicate injection cases were also run. The errors cluster around reload: the `hassette reload` command does not exist, and reload creates a new instance with an empty job registry, so if_exists is not what makes on_initialize safe to re-run. There is also one minor overstatement of what the job detail view renders.
